independence_scope: intra-mesh Anthropic-family; agreement is corroboration, never cross-provider evidence

reviews.reasoning: Ps 78 is an identity psalm (72 WEB verses = 72 MT verses, rule 'identity' in web_mt_offset_map.json), so oshb: cites in this cluster map 1:1 to their web: refs and no shift arithmetic applies; I re-derived that before ruling on any citation. Opening seam 51|52 re-checked in both witnesses: MT Ps.78.51 closes the Egypt strike on בְּאָהֳלֵי חָֽם and MT Ps.78.52 opens with a fronted causative wayyiqtol וַיַּסַּ֣ע governing a new object, which WEB carries in parallel -- “and struck all the firstborn in Egypt, the chief of their strength in the tents of Ham.” (web:Ps.78.51) then “But he led out his own people like sheep, and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.” (web:Ps.78.52). That is a tier-1 subject-and-scene shift and the span opening is sound. The closing seam is equally sound: MT Ps.78.55 ends on the settled state וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֥ן בְּ֝אָהֳלֵיהֶ֗ם שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל and MT Ps.78.56 opens the next cycle with the wayyiqtol pair וַיְנַסּ֣וּ וַ֭יַּמְרוּ. The row's 1 Hebrew citation collates at byte tier at its cited ref (collate.py, oshb:Ps.78.52 -> byte), and its 6 WEB quotations check clean at check_web_quotes. Two observations that are not defects: the paseq inventory in pmarks_Ps.json records a paseq seg at MT Ps.78.55 (seg layer, single-witness, tier-3 at most), which the row neither cites nor needs; and כַּ֝עֵ֗דֶר (oshb:Ps.78.52, byte tier) is a 1-verse form book-wide (skeleton sweep, unit = verses), a sharper unused signal than the one the row leaned on. The span, the parent and the unit type are right; what I contest is the novelty framing carrying the row's lead substrate signal.

challenges.claim: The row's lead substrate signal calls וַיַּסַּ֣ע (oshb:Ps.78.52) a new verb of departure/leading, but the same hiphil-nun-samekh-ayin plus nun-he-gimel verb pair already stands, in the same two colon positions, at oshb:Ps.78.26 inside this psalm, and the novelty is asserted with 0 supporting sweep digits.
challenges.evidence: Spliced byte-true from verse_map_oshb.json and re-collated rather than typed. oshb:Ps.78.52 opens וַיַּסַּ֣ע and turns at וַֽיְנַהֲגֵ֥ם; oshb:Ps.78.26 opens יַסַּ֣ע and turns at וַיְנַהֵ֖ג -- the verbs sit at token 0 and token 3 of the bicolon in both verses, and both strings collate at byte tier at their own refs (collate.py). Sweeps with the unit named: skeleton nun-he-gimel returns 4 verses book-wide, 2 of them in this psalm (Ps.78.26, Ps.78.52); the skeleton for the causative of nun-samekh-ayin returns 2 verses in this psalm (Ps.78.26, Ps.78.52) once the book's samekh-ayin-dalet substring noise is discarded by pointed byte check per verse. Both witnesses read the pair causatively at the 2 sites: WEB “He caused the east wind to blow in the sky. By his power he guided the south wind.” (web:Ps.78.26) against “But he led out his own people like sheep, and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.” (web:Ps.78.52). Ps 78 is identity, so web:Ps.78.26 = oshb:Ps.78.26 and web:Ps.78.52 = oshb:Ps.78.52. The row's narrower qualifier -- absence from the plagues catalogue at Ps.78.43-51 -- does hold (0 verses in that stretch carry either root), so the 51|52 seam survives intact; what fails is the unswept word 'new', which a reader takes at psalm scope, and the undisclosed ordered pair at Ps.78.26 is the exact echo that framing denies.

reviews.reasoning: Seams re-checked in both witnesses. Opening seam 55|56: MT Ps.78.55 closes on וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֥ן בְּ֝אָהֳלֵיהֶ֗ם שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל and MT Ps.78.56 opens וַיְנַסּ֣וּ וַ֭יַּמְרוּ, a tier-1 subject shift that WEB carries with its adversative -- “Yet they tempted and rebelled against the Most High God, and didn't keep his testimonies,” (web:Ps.78.56). Closing seam 64|65 is sound: MT Ps.78.64 ends וְ֝אַלְמְנֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א תִבְכֶּֽינָה and MT Ps.78.65 opens the reversal with וַיִּקַ֖ץ. The row's 2 Hebrew citations collate at byte tier at oshb:Ps.78.56 (collate.py). I re-derived both digits and both hold as scoped: the tempting-verb form stands in 3 verses of this psalm (Ps.78.18, Ps.78.41, Ps.78.56) at accent_stripped and skeleton tiers, and the divine title stands in 3 verses of this psalm (Ps.78.17, Ps.78.35, Ps.78.56) at skeleton tier. Two tier facts the row leaves unnamed without misstating them: at byte tier the accented form quoted from oshb:Ps.78.56 stands in 2 verses of this psalm (Ps.78.41, Ps.78.56), because oshb:Ps.78.18 carries the unaccented וַיְנַסּוּ -- the staged extract serializes maqaf as space, so that token lost its conjunctive accent along with its maqaf -- and book-wide the same form reaches 4 verses. Since the row scopes both counts to this psalm and names its objects as a form and a title rather than as byte strings, neither count is wrong. The rejected_alternative also verifies: MT Ps.78.60 opens with the wayyiqtol וַ֭יִּטֹּשׁ, a continuation form rather than an opening marker, so declining the 59|60 cut is correct. My challenge is confined to the unswept half of the verb pair the row builds its opening warrant on.

challenges.claim: The row's opening warrant rests on a two-verb convergence but sweeps 1 of the 2 members: the tempting-verb carries a 3-verse digit while the rebelling-verb is left unswept, and the 2 anchors named for the rebelling side skip Ps.78.17, which is the psalm's other mem-resh-he site and the 1 that already collocates that root with the divine title the row sweeps in its next signal.
challenges.evidence: Swept per attested spelling (sweep.py --skel, unit = verses), then confirmed from pointed bytes because those skeleton substrings over-match unrelated roots elsewhere in the book. The mem-resh-he root stands in 4 verses of this psalm: וּמֹ֫רֶ֥ה (oshb:Ps.78.8), לַֽמְר֥וֹת (oshb:Ps.78.17), יַמְר֣וּהוּ (oshb:Ps.78.40), וַ֭יַּמְרוּ (oshb:Ps.78.56), with byte-tier collation at their own refs (collate.py). The row names 2 of those 4. The skipped verse is the closest parallel to the span opening: oshb:Ps.78.17 reads לַֽמְר֥וֹת עֶ֝לְי֗וֹן and oshb:Ps.78.56 reads וַ֭יַּמְרוּ ... עֶלְי֑וֹן, so Ps.78.17 is the 1 other verse in this psalm where the rebelling root governs that title. Ps.78.8 is also the weaker of the 2 named anchors: its וּמֹ֫רֶ֥ה sits inside the noun phrase דּוֹר֮ סוֹרֵ֪ר וּמֹ֫רֶ֥ה, characterizing the fathers' generation, rather than functioning as a finite verb of the people's rebelling the way Ps.78.40 and Ps.78.56 do. Ps 78 is identity, so web:Ps.78.17 = oshb:Ps.78.17. Filed at low because disclosure strengthens rather than reverses the row: Ps.78.17-18 spreads over 2 verses what Ps.78.56 compresses into 1 clause, which is the row's own third-cycle reading.

reviews.reasoning: Closing arithmetic re-derived: Ps 78 runs 72 verses in both witnesses, so the span end at Ps.78.72 is the psalm end and the row does not cross a psalm boundary; across this cluster the tiling of Ps.78.52-Ps.78.72 is exact (21 verses expected, 21 covered, 0 gaps, 0 overlaps, check_tiling.py). The 64|65 seam verifies as stated above. The row's strongest signal survives re-derivation at the 3 tiers collate.py reports: וַיִּקַ֖ץ (oshb:Ps.78.65) returns 1 verse book-wide at byte, at accent_stripped and at skeleton, so the hapax-in-this-book claim is robust rather than tier-dependent, and the object it names -- the verb form -- is the recoverable one of the 3 words quoted. I also tested the divine-name question WEB's rendering raises here: MT Ps.78.65 reads אֲדֹנָ֑י, so “Then the Lord awakened as one out of sleep, like a mighty man who shouts by reason of wine.” (web:Ps.78.65) is a straight rendering of the MT reading and not the 68:26 rendering zone; nothing is owed in disclosure and the row is right to stay silent. The row's third signal -- that the closing shepherd material answers the flock simile without repeating its wording -- does hold in Hebrew for Ps.78.71-72, which use לִ֭רְעוֹת (oshb:Ps.78.71), וַ֭יִּרְעֵם and יַנְחֵֽם (oshb:Ps.78.72) against Ps.78.52's וַֽיְנַהֲגֵ֥ם, כַּצֹּ֣אן and כַּ֝עֵ֗דֶר. Worth recording for the seam file: the same claim argued from the English would fail, since WEB renders the 2 different verbs alike -- “and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.” (web:Ps.78.52) against “and guided them by the skillfulness of his hands.” (web:Ps.78.72) -- and it is the Hebrew that rescues the row. I file 2 challenges, on the Ephraim count-object and on an undisclosed repetition inside the row's own span; the span itself, the parent and the confidence stand.

challenges.claim: The row's Ephraim sweep names its count-object as the byte-tier-cited token itself -- '2 verses in this psalm carry אֶ֝פְרַ֗יִם (oshb:Ps.78.67, byte tier)' -- but that byte string stands in 1 verse book-wide; the 2-verse frame count holds at accent_stripped and skeleton tiers, not at the tier the row names.
challenges.evidence: Spliced from verse_map_oshb.json, not typed. oshb:Ps.78.67 token 4 is אֶ֝פְרַ֗יִם, codepoints 05D0 05B6 059D 05E4 05B0 05E8 05B7 0597 05D9 05B4 05DD; oshb:Ps.78.9 token 1 is אֶפְרַ֗יִם, codepoints 05D0 05B6 05E4 05B0 05E8 05B7 0597 05D9 05B4 05DD. The 78:67 token carries U+059D telisha qetana after the segol and the 78:9 token does not, so the 2 strings are not byte-equal. sweep.py on the 78:67 byte string returns byte = 1 verse (Ps.78.67); sweep.py on the 78:9 byte string returns byte = 1 verse (Ps.78.9); the skeleton for that name returns 5 verses book-wide, 2 of them in this psalm (Ps.78.9, Ps.78.67). Unit = verses throughout, and collate.py confirms the 2 tokens at byte tier at their own refs. Ps 78 is identity, so web:Ps.78.9 = oshb:Ps.78.9 and web:Ps.78.67 = oshb:Ps.78.67. The frame the row argues is real at lexeme level and the span is unaffected, so this is a count-object defect rather than a warrant defect -- but the count as written is false at the tier the row itself names. The same row's Ps.78.65 signal shows the cure: it names its object as a verb form and survives at 3 tiers.

challenges.claim: The row states that the closing shepherd material answers the flock simile of Ps.78.52 without repeating its wording, but Ps.78.70 -- inside this row's own span -- recovers that simile's noun as צֹֽאן (oshb:Ps.78.70) and the row does not disclose it.
challenges.evidence: sweep.py --skel on the noun returns 15 verses book-wide, 2 of them in this psalm: Ps.78.52 and Ps.78.70 (unit = verses). Spliced byte-true: oshb:Ps.78.52 token 1 is כַּצֹּ֣אן and oshb:Ps.78.70 token 5 is צֹֽאן, both collating at byte tier at their own refs (collate.py). WEB carries the same recovery -- “But he led out his own people like sheep, and guided them in the wilderness like a flock.” (web:Ps.78.52) against “He also chose David his servant, and took him from the sheepfolds;” (web:Ps.78.70). Ps 78 is identity, so web:Ps.78.70 = oshb:Ps.78.70. The row's claim survives strictly under its stated scope of Ps.78.71-72, but the row's device_notes then widens the same relation to the shepherd image closing the psalm without carrying the qualifier, and the 1 verse that repeats the simile's noun sits between them. Filed at low because the recovery at Ps.78.70 corroborates the row's frame reading rather than contradicting it: it needs disclosing, not reversing.
